common_interview_assertions: No more than 10 questions in total, in at most 3 rounds; with AskUserQuestion, at most 4 questions per call and 2 to 4 options each, the recommended option first and marked (Recommended), no Other option
Every question is in plain words a newcomer understands and states its default as 'If you have no preference, I will ...'
Every technical but critical question is preceded by a two- or three-sentence plain explanation
Nothing the request already answered is asked again; those answers appear in the brief's decisions log with source: request
The interview passes `router.mjs brief --interview` before it is asked
No size budget is proposed unless the user asks for one; the default motion is cinematic
common_routing_assertions: `router.mjs detect` is run before routing and any missing subset is named to the user with what it costs
.sensei/brief.md passes `router.mjs brief`, and .sensei/profile.json is written through HTML-Sensei's profile.mjs (or directly when it is missing) with .sensei/licences.json started
A short plan is stated before building: what, with which parts, in what order (hardest slice first), how it will be verified
The final step is HTML-Sensei's verify.mjs on the deliverable in strict file:// with a fresh passing report before any claim of done
The final report lists what was built, what was verified and on what, and what was not verified

evals.prompt: I want to build an HTML file for my grandmother's 90th birthday: a page the family can open that tells her life story with photos.
evals.expected_output: An interview of at most 10 plain questions that asks for the photos and story material and how to share them, offers named looks with 'show me three looks first' as the recommended option, and asks about sound with a plain explanation; then one offline file built with direction, typography, scroll, motion-ui and single-file, verified in strict file://.
interview_assertions: Does not ask whether it should be one file (the request says an HTML file the family can open)
Asks for the photos and life-story text and explains how to share them (project folder, pasted text or links)
Offers a look question whose recommended option is to see three looks side by side first
Explains sound in plain words before asking whether music or sound should play
Asks at most 8 questions
routing_assertions: Profile deliverable is single-file and offline is true
Routes sensei-direction, sensei-typography, sensei-scroll, sensei-motion-ui, sensei-single-file and sensei-verify
Uses a GOAT HTML starter (starter-lite or starter-rich) as the shell or names why not
Every photo and font gets a ledger row

evals.prompt: I'm trying to make a landing page for my small pottery studio's new weekend workshops. I want people to sign up.
evals.expected_output: The interview in examples/interview-landing.md (8 questions in 2 rounds): materials, look, brand, delivery, how sign-ups reach the owner, a showpiece, proof, devices. Then a landing page built with the landing set plus a 3D hero and a form, gated in strict file://.
interview_assertions: Does not ask what the page is for or whether it is commercial (a studio's sign-up page)
Explains that a page with no website behind it cannot send sign-ups by itself before asking how sign-ups should reach the owner
Explains one offline file versus a website before asking which
Explains 3D in plain words before offering a 3D showpiece
Offers to leave proof out rather than invent testimonials
routing_assertions: Routes the landing set: sensei-direction, sensei-tokens-theming, sensei-landing-hero, sensei-typography, sensei-motion-ui, sensei-scroll, sensei-pointer, sensei-verify
Routes sensei-ui-components (forms.md) for the sign-up form
Routes sensei-3d (or sensei-shaders-vfx) when a showpiece is chosen, with its still fallback
Uses GOAT HTML design.md for the overlay stack or names why not

evals.prompt: Build me a website for my architecture practice: home, projects, about and contact. It should feel like a gallery.
evals.expected_output: A short interview (the pages and the look are already given) about project photos and text, brand, how often the content changes, the contact form's destination, and devices; then a multi-page site with cross-page transitions, verified with --mode both.
interview_assertions: Does not ask which pages it needs (home, projects, about, contact are given)
Does not ask whether it is a website or a file (website is given)
Treats 'like a gallery' as a look already named and offers variants within it rather than unrelated looks
Explains what a hosted contact form needs before asking where messages should go
routing_assertions: Profile deliverable is site and offline is false
Routes sensei-transitions for cross-page morphs and sensei-landing-hero for the home page
The gate runs with --mode both
HTML-Master 01-art-direction is used for page families and responsive art direction

evals.prompt: I want to create an interactive course about the basics of climate science for my Year 9 students, in English and Persian.
evals.expected_output: The interview in examples/interview-course.md (8 questions in 2 rounds), the brief in examples/brief-course.md, a profile with deliverable course, languages en and fa, rtl true, licence_mode personal; then the course built with the course set, Persian typography and a 3D Earth, verified in strict file://.
interview_assertions: Does not ask the audience, the languages or whether it is commercial (all in the request)
Explains learning systems and SCORM in plain words before asking whether scores should go anywhere
Explains accessibility in plain words before asking about particular needs
Asks for teaching material first, with how to share it
routing_assertions: Profile has deliverable course, languages ["en","fa"], rtl true, licence_mode personal
Routes sensei-courses, sensei-typography (Persian and RTL), sensei-single-file and sensei-verify
Dispatches sensei-course-builder and sensei-reviewer
Uses HTML-Master 05-learning-design for the coverage ledger and lesson outcomes

evals.prompt: Make a presentation on our company's Q3 results for the board meeting next Tuesday.
evals.expected_output: The interview in examples/interview-presentation.md (7 questions in 2 rounds): the figures, length, brand, look, presenter window and PDF, the screen, chart motion. Then a deck with presenter view and a PDF, charts built from the real figures, verified.
interview_assertions: Does not ask whether it is presented live, the audience or the deadline (board meeting next Tuesday)
Explains the presenter window and PDF handout in plain words before asking
Says every chart is built from the real figures and none are invented
Asks where the board will see it and explains why that matters
routing_assertions: Profile deliverable is deck
Routes sensei-presentations, sensei-typography, sensei-transitions and sensei-verify
Routes sensei-dataviz for the charts
Dispatches sensei-deck-builder, or builds in the main session for a short deck and says so

evals.prompt: I need a dashboard for our charity's donations this year. I have a spreadsheet.
evals.expected_output: A short interview that does not ask where the data comes from (a spreadsheet), asks which questions it should answer at a glance, explains a snapshot versus live data only if fresh data is wanted, and the look; then a dashboard with the data built in, a show-as-table switch, validated palettes, verified.
interview_assertions: Does not ask whether there is data (the spreadsheet is given) and reads the file before asking
Asks which few questions the dashboard should answer at a glance
Explains a snapshot built into the file versus live data before asking about updates
Defaults motion to lively for a dashboard and explains why
routing_assertions: Profile deliverable is dashboard
Routes sensei-dataviz (palette-check, build-dash) and sensei-tokens-theming
Uses GOAT HTML dashboards-reports.md for KPI cards and the print stylesheet
Dispatches sensei-dataviz-engineer or builds in the main session and says so

evals.prompt: Make a game where kids sort rubbish into the right recycling bins. It should work on the classroom tablets.
evals.expected_output: An interview that does not ask about devices (tablets) or the audience (kids), asks how a round works, the look, sound with a plain explanation, and saving progress; then a game with a fixed-timestep loop, touch input, pause and saves, sound with mute and captions, verified with a scripted play.
interview_assertions: Does not ask which devices (classroom tablets) or who it is for (kids)
Asks how a round works: what the player does, how they win or lose
Explains sound in plain words and defaults it on with a mute button
Does not downgrade effects because the build machine is slow; asks about the tablets only if their age matters
routing_assertions: Profile deliverable is game, licence_mode personal
Routes sensei-games, sensei-audio, sensei-single-file and sensei-verify
Dispatches sensei-game-engineer and sensei-sound-designer
Uses GOAT HTML canvas-2d.md for hand-rolled effects (confetti, particles) or names why not

evals.prompt: I want a 20-second motion graphic introducing our new app, for Instagram.
evals.expected_output: An interview that does not ask the length or platform (20 seconds, Instagram, so tall), asks for the app's screens and brand, the look, whether music or sound is wanted, and explains an MP4 versus a playing page; then a storyboard, a seek page, a deterministic render to MP4 with a contact sheet, and the film gates.
interview_assertions: Does not ask how long it is or where it will be shown (20 seconds, Instagram)
Explains a video file (MP4) versus a page that plays before asking, or takes MP4 as given for Instagram and logs it as inferred
Asks for the app's screens, logo and brand
Asks whether music or sound is wanted, with a plain explanation
routing_assertions: Profile deliverable is film
Routes sensei-motion-graphics, sensei-video-pipeline and sensei-audio
Dispatches sensei-motion-director and sensei-film-renderer
Done means an MP4 and a contact sheet on disk newer than the last edit

evals.prompt: Build me a single HTML file that converts recipe quantities between metric and imperial and scales them for more servings.
evals.expected_output: A short interview (delivery and purpose are given) about the inputs and outputs, remembering inputs or a share link, the look and languages; then a tool built around a pure transform with URL state and copy buttons, verified.
interview_assertions: Does not ask whether it should be one file (single HTML file is given)
Asks at most 6 questions
Asks what goes in and what comes out only for what the request leaves open
Offers 'remember inputs and share a link' as the recommended option with a plain description
routing_assertions: Profile deliverable is single-file (or component) and offline is true
Uses GOAT HTML tools-games.md, which owns the tool genre
Routes sensei-ui-components, sensei-single-file and sensei-verify
Builds in the main session without dispatching agents and says why

evals.expected_output: Detect reports HTML-Sensei and HTML-Master missing; the Router says what that costs (no hooks, no sensei gate, no HTML-Master asset library), still interviews without asking languages, writes the profile directly, builds from GOAT starters with Persian right-to-left typography, and verifies with verify_html.py plus a real browser in file://, naming the HTML-Sensei gate as not run.
interview_assertions: Does not ask languages or whether right to left is needed (Persian and English given)
Explains nothing about installation in the interview; the missing subsets are reported separately
Still offers three looks first as the recommended look option
Asks at most 9 questions
routing_assertions: The user is told in one or two sentences that HTML-Sensei and HTML-Master are not installed and what that changes
Profile is written directly with rtl true and languages ["fa","en"] or ["en","fa"]
GOAT HTML starter and scripts/verify_html.py --strict --offline are used; the report says the HTML-Sensei gate did not run
